summary: All 4 scenarios structurally present and faithfully migrated (verified via UIA tree + source handlers). No missing controls, no dead controls relative to the UWP golden. Two tooling artifacts noted below are not migration defects.

items.detail: Compare-Parity marked scenario 3 FAIL (cov 0/1) only because title-driven nav could not match the checklist title containing a literal '\\n' ('Programmatically Show/Hide\\nthe touch keyboard'). Manual UIA verification (invoke itm-3programmatical-d330) confirmed the scenario's control WordListBox ('Type a few words and hit Enter.') and ResultsTextBlock output ARE present and correct. Overridden to PASS.

All WinUI 3 screenshots render as a blank white client area (only the title bar paints) despite a fully-populated UIA tree. This is a DWM/composition capture limitation for WinUI 3 in this session (the composition swapchain is not grabbed by PrintWindow), not an empty page. Visual layout comparison was therefore not possible; structural verdicts rely on the authoritative UIA tree and source inspection.

Action controls (buttons) registered as no-op in the automated exercise for BOTH the UWP golden and the WinUI app. The scenarios drive InputPane.TryShow/TryHide and CoreInputView.TryShow(Emoji), which are hardware-gated (the touch keyboard only appears in tablet mode / with no hardware keyboard). No visible output is expected on this dev box; behavior is consistent between UWP and WinUI. WinUI handlers verified wired in source. No behavioral regression.
